rendered:
The document "Energy and environmental aspects in recycling lithium-ion batteries: Concept of Battery Identity Global Passport" (mattod-2020) cites a froth flotation study. 

The collector used in the study was kerosene. 
Over 90% of the spent graphite floated in the froth layers. 
The cathode tailing product had a purity of 88.2% and a total recovery of 74.3%.

prompt.system: You answer questions using only the documents below: pages selected from them, with tables written row by row. Answer briefly. If you compute a number, show the calculation. If the question assumes something the documents contradict, say so. If the documents do not hold the answer, say so.

expect: kerosene; over 90% of spent graphite floated; tailing with 88.2% active cathode materials at a total recovery of 74.3% (p7.L97-101)
question: In the froth flotation study the review cites, what collector was used, what share of the graphite floated, and what purity and total recovery did the cathode tailing product reach?
